ai.description: *Ahaetulla anomala* (Colubridae) is a slender, vine-like snake reaching 1.2 meters. It is bright green with a distinct horizontal pupil and a pointed snout, lacking the dark mid-dorsal line of similar species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ahaetulla anomala* is best distinguished by its distinctively short, blunt snout and a lack of a prominent rostral appendage, unlike the elongated snouts of other *Ahaetulla* species.
ai.habitat: *Ahaetulla anomala* inhabits dense evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in the mid-canopy and shrub layers at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.behavior: *Ahaetulla anomala* is primarily diurnal and uses its slender, cryptic body to remain motionless among foliage, effectively camouflaging itself while hunting for small prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ahaetulla anomala* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–9 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April to August) in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ahaetulla anomala* is found in the Western Ghats of India, spanning states like Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
